chunks: Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who made a bequest of his wealth in the way of Allah.
So he said: "Give it to the one for whom he made the bequest, even if he is a Jew or a Christian. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:"
"But whoever changes it after hearing it, then its sin is only upon those who change it."

key_terms.أَوْصَى بِمَالِهِ: made a bequest concerning his wealth
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: in the way of Allah; for a cause dedicated to Allah

ai.seo_question: Must an Islamic bequest be fulfilled exactly as stated, even if the beneficiary is a Jew or a Christian?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a valid bequest must be carried out as the deceased specified, without altering it. The Imam عليه السلام affirms that this applies even if the beneficiary is a Jew or a Christian, and supports the ruling with the Qur'anic prohibition against changing a bequest after hearing it.
